item.title: Motion on the Organisation of a Freshers’ Fair on the St James’ Campus Passes at Comhairle 6
item.description: On March 10th, a motion was brought to Comhairle 6 to mandate the organisation of a Freshers’ Fair on the St James’s Hospital campus. The motion was proposed by Trinity College Dublin Students’ Union (TCDSU/AMLCT) President Grace McNally and seconded by Ents Officer, Orla Norton. item.title: Motion to Establish a National Network of International Student Reps Passes
item.description: A motion to establish a nationwide network of student representatives has passed at this week’s Comhairle. The motion, proposed by International Officer Aman Bansal, intends to connect international student representatives across Irish colleges by establishing a shared network on which they can exchange information and share advice. item.title: Writer, Actor and Comedian John Mulaney Receives Honorary Patronage from the Phil
item.description: On Tuesday, March 10th, John Mulaney, prominent American comedian and producer, received the University Philosophical Society (the Phil) Medal of Honorary Patronage in the GMB debate chamber. Liam Corcoran, President of the Phil, presented the award and emphasised the Phil’s formal recognition of Mulaney’s remarkable achievements in the field of comedy, paying tribute to the “warmth and affability” with which Mulaney approaches his work. item.title: A Reflection on the Legacy of Boycotting in Ireland

item.title: Scrambler Ban Risks Repeating Ireland’s Enforcement Problem
item.description: Following the death of Grace Lynch, the Government has promised a “total ban” on scrambler bikes. This may seem like a great solution to all the public nuisance they have been causing, however on closer look we see a familiar trend in Irish policymaking: the gap between the law on the books and the law in practice, and the political temptation to close this gap with new wording as opposed to sustained enforcement. item.title: Trinity People Before Profit Implement Permanent Vegan Policy
item.description: On Tuesday March 10th Trinity People Before Profit (TCD PBP) announced they were implementing a permanent vegan policy and urged the Trinity College Students’ Union (TCDSU), other societies and Trinity College Dublin itself to take on similar policies. The policy mandates that all future society activities or events will have no animal products purchased nor served. item.title: TCD Women’s Health, DUDJ, DUPA, Trinity VDP, and FLAC Win Big at the Society of the Year Awards
